findings.finding: LoanSet first checks ordinary transaction authorization. When Counterparty is the LoanBroker Owner, Account is the borrower and the owner is the independently checked counter signer.

After fixCleanup3_4_0, a single counterparty signature uses CPT (0x43505400) plus canonical signing-field serialization; borrower multisigning uses SMT (0x534D5400), the same body, and each signer AccountID suffix.
CounterpartySignature and Signers are kNotSigning, so the two signature containers do not enter either signing body and can coexist.
PrincipalRequested is a required LoanSet signing field. Changing it after broker authorization invalidates that authorization and changes disbursement, principal, Vault assets, and Loan Broker debt.
fixCleanup3_4_0 replaces the shared legacy role prefix with distinct transaction, counterparty, and sponsor domains; E6 requires the fixed counterparty domain.
LendingProtocolV1_1 rejects Subscription with tecTOO_SOON and Redemption with tecEXPIRED and requires the Investment schedule to leave the redemption buffer.

Successful LoanSet disburses principal, creates the Loan from LoanBrokerID and pre-increment LoanSequence, updates cash-basis Vault availability, broker debt/owner count/sequence, and borrower ownership.
The Loan index is SHA-512Half over namespace L, LoanBrokerID, and LoanSequence.
A fresh LEVersion 1 Vault uses cash-basis origination: AssetsTotal is unchanged and DebtTotal increases by principal.
Pinned tests demonstrate that fixCleanup3_4_0 rejects copying a valid counterparty signature into another authorization role.
